label: Early original-phase step (t=1-2) where a token from {e,y,d,w,h,m} follows one of {0,y,m,b,w,d}
explanation: Low end of candidate unit 118. About 76% of activation mass falls in the original phase, mostly at t=1-3 (41% at t=1, 27% at t=2). It never fires at t=0 and almost never at orig_idx>=4. Within these early steps it depends on the bigram: current input in {e,y,d,w,h,m} and previous input in {0,y,m,b,w,d}. The strongest activations come from sequences that start with 0 (e.g. 0 0 e, 0 0 y) or start with z/1 followed by y/d. At t==1 the bigram rule has 95% precision but only 30% recall. Over t=1-2 the predicate reaches dev F1 0.51 (precision 0.66, recall 0.41, mass recall 0.54). The remaining mass is spread thinly: weak firing at the <DEL> step of short (L=3) sequences, at the first copy step, and a diffuse tail of low activations in the middle copy phase (recall_idx 2-5) with no clear token rule. Position alone (t=1-3) has very low precision (3%), so the token context is essential. Treat this as only a partial description of a hidden-state-dependent unit.
